topics.title: 11.1 TCP/IP Fundamentals
topics.summary: A network protocol is an agreed way to exchange information. IP delivers packets between addresses. TCP adds a reliable, ordered byte stream between endpoints; UDP sends independent datagrams without TCP’s connection and delivery mechanisms. Applications build their own messages on top. HTTP over TCP, for example, is not the same layer as the IP route carrying it.

blocks.text: A network protocol is an agreed way to exchange information. IP delivers packets between addresses. TCP adds a reliable, ordered byte stream between endpoints; UDP sends independent datagrams without TCP’s connection and delivery mechanisms. Applications build their own messages on top. HTTP over TCP, for example, is not the same layer as the IP route carrying it.

Think of an endpoint as an address, transport protocol, and port. TCP port 443 and UDP port 443 are different endpoints. A successful ping does not prove that either accepts an application request. Conversely, a blocked ping does not prove the web service is unavailable. Choose a test that matches the layer and protocol under investigation.

topics.title: 11.3 MAC Addresses
topics.summary: An Ethernet MAC address identifies a link-layer interface on a local network. IPv4 neighbors commonly resolve an IP address to a MAC address through ARP; IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery. Routers replace link-layer addressing as traffic moves between links, so the remote internet server’s MAC address does not normally appear in your local neighbor table.

blocks.text: An Ethernet MAC address identifies a link-layer interface on a local network. IPv4 neighbors commonly resolve an IP address to a MAC address through ARP; IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery. Inspect neighbors with ip neigh. An incomplete or failed entry can point toward an unreachable local neighbor, but first confirm that the selected route expects that neighbor on this link. Virtual machines, bonding, and address changes complicate identity. A familiar MAC address is not an authentication mechanism.

topics.summary: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses. It supports multiple address scopes, including link-local addresses that normally begin with fe80. Do not disable IPv6 as a reflexive troubleshooting step. A hostname can return both A and AAAA records, and an application may choose either family. topics.title: 11.6 CIDR and Subnetting
topics.summary: CIDR writes an address followed by its prefix length, such as /24. A longer prefix describes a smaller address range. For ordinary IPv4 broadcast subnets, a /26 has 64 addresses, with conventional network and broadcast reservations leaving 62 host addresses. Special-purpose prefixes, including /31 point-to-point links, require different assumptions.

topics.title: 11.7 Default Gateways
topics.summary: A default gateway is the next hop used when no more specific route matches a destination. It is not necessarily the address ending in .1. It must be reachable according to the interface and route configuration, and the router must know how to forward the traffic onward.

labs.title: Distinguish connectivity from listening service
labs.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
lab_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$lab_dir"' EXIT
cd -- "$lab_dir"
printf 'route=present\nlistener=absent\n' > network.fixture
grep -qx 'route=present' network.fixture
grep -qx 'listener=absent' network.fixture
printf 'route evidence present; listener still missing\n'
